reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Living donor kidney transplant recipient who missed his Monday dialysis: K 6.1 to 6.2 with new peaked T waves, 4 kg over dry weight with pulmonary congestion, pH 7.30, gastroparesis requiring RSI, while his brother's donor nephrectomy is scheduled to induce at 0730.

asa.rationale: ESRD with hyperkalemia, volume overload, diabetic complications.

decision.recommendation: delay the recipient for dialysis and hold the donor induction
decision.rationale: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes plus volume overload before a case that needs volume loading at reperfusion is unsafe. Call the transplant attending and donor room immediately so the donor is not induced; dialyze the recipient first (a few hours).

redFlags.evidence: K 6.1 and POC 6.2; new peaked T V2 to V5; missed HD 10/26; no hyperkalemia treatment ordered.
redFlags.implication: Arrhythmia, worsened by acidosis, succinylcholine, reperfusion.
redFlags.action: Preop dialysis; if emergent: calcium, insulin with dextrose, avoid succinylcholine, avoid hypoventilation.

redFlags.evidence: +4 kg over EDW, crackles, SpO2 94%, new vascular congestion and effusions, BP 172/98.
redFlags.implication: Pulmonary edema with intraop volume loading for graft perfusion.

redFlags.evidence: Donor induction 0730 in OR 22; fellow says proceed.
redFlags.implication: A healthy donor exposed to surgery with a recipient not ready.
redFlags.action: Escalate to the transplant attending before donor induction.
RSI with rocuronium (succinylcholine contraindicated at this K).

redFlags.implication: No cuff, IV or arterial line on left.

planItems.item: Dialysis to normalize K and volume before surgery
Volume load to CVP 10 to 12, mannitol and furosemide at reperfusion
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
